problem: Find $(3a+b)\cdot c+(2b-2c)\cdot d,$ if $c\cdot a=3,$ $c\cdot b=-2,$ $b\cdot d=-1,$ and $d\cdot c=2.$
worked_solution:
Using the fact that the dot product is linear in the first variable, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(3a+b)\cdot c+(2b-2c)\cdot d & =(3a)\cdot c+b\cdot c+(2b)\cdot d-(2c)\cdot d \\  & =3(a\cdot c)+b\cdot c+2(b\cdot d)-2(c\cdot d).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we can use the fact that the dot product is symmetric to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3(a\cdot c)+b\cdot c+2(b\cdot d)-2(c\cdot d) & =3(c\cdot a)+c\cdot b+2(b\cdot d)-2(d\cdot c).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting the values for $c\cdot a,$ $c\cdot b,$ $b\cdot d,$ and $d\cdot c,$ we find

$$
\begin{aligned}3(c\cdot a)+c\cdot b+2(b\cdot d)-2(d\cdot c) & =3(3)+(-2)+2(-1)-2(2) \\  & =9-2-2-4 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $(3a+b)\cdot c+(2b-2c)\cdot d=1.$
